title: The Things I Let Him See
logline:
A surveillance operative hired to prove a separated wife unstable becomes
obsessed with her ordinary routines, unaware that she identified him almost
immediately and has begun designing what he sees.

When her husband's domestic gaslighting escalates toward a forced property
settlement, the watcher must decide whether to possess the woman directing
his gaze or preserve the evidence that will return her life to her.

content_rules: No secret twin, impostor, body double, memory-loss twist, hidden pregnancy, or false identity twist.
No hallucination explanation for Lena's observations.
No hidden camera inside Lena's apartment; no bedroom or bathroom recording; no recording of nudity or sexual activity.
No sexual assault presented as romance; no sexual contact before the Chapter Ten rules.
No gun, knife, kidnapping, physical assault, chase climax, or violent rescue.
No hacker friend, secret server, unexplained cloud backup, mystery USB drive, or surprise forensic device.
No new evidence introduced after Chapter Fifteen.
No scene outside Calder's POV; no omniscient action by Grant or Lena.
No police action based on one recording or accusation; no detective attending the confidential settlement without a declared legal reason; no instant arrest during the settlement scene.
No instant divorce judgment, property transfer, or criminal conviction.
No named character outside the locked cast; no child, pregnancy, or custody subplot.
No mafia, organized crime, billionaire fantasy, cult, or international conspiracy.
No redemption for Grant; no revelation that Calder designed Lena's counterstrategy.
No romance payoff for Calder ignoring Lena's refusal; no Book Two villain physically appearing in Book One.
No version of the climax requiring Grant to confess that he stole the envelope.
No portrayal of Lena's Chapter Eight action as certainty that Calder recorded the envelope theft.
